overview: The Medford School Committee approved submitting an MSBA Statement of Interest for vocational school renovations and authorized computer-based PARCC testing for Andrews Middle School. The committee also reviewed updates on state opiate legislation compliance, access television studio construction, elementary health awards, and school maintenance.

items.title: Approval of Minutes, Payrolls, and Reports
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes of March 7, 2016, the district payrolls, and the Committee of the Whole report from March 9, 2016.

items.title: EOS Healthy Start Award Report
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent Diane Caldwell reported that Columbus Elementary School received a 5-year award and $500 for achieving over 80% student participation in its universal free breakfast program.

items.title: PARCC/MCAS Testing Schedule and Opt-Out Guidance
items.summary: Curriculum Director Bernadette Ricciardelli presented testing schedules and state opt-out guidance, leading the committee to approve computer-based PARCC testing for Andrews Middle School and request a post-testing report on opt-out numbers.

items.title: Motion on Tracking Pending Agenda Items
items.summary: The committee approved a motion to list pending and tabled items on future meeting agendas to track requested reports and documents.

items.title: MSBA Statement of Interest for Vocational High School
items.summary: Vocational Director Dr. Heidi Riccio presented a plan to submit an MSBA Statement of Interest under Priority 7 for space reorganization, ADA upgrades, and STEM lab expansion, which the committee approved.

items.title: Multimedia Community Access Channel Construction Status
items.summary: Dr. Heidi Riccio reported that asbestos abatement for the new community access television studio will occur during April vacation, with main construction taking place over the summer for a planned September 2016 opening.

items.title: Opiate Legislation (House 4056) and District Implementation
items.summary: Superintendent Belson outlined district steps to comply with state opiate legislation, including school nurse Narcan training, plans for student screening, and expansion of the Michigan Model health curriculum.

items.title: Brooks Elementary School Maintenance Report
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent Caldwell detailed a March 9 sewage backup caused by paper towels in the waste line, which temporarily closed the Brooks kitchen for cleaning, wallboard replacement, and Board of Health re-inspection.

items.title: Announcements and Executive Session
items.summary: Following brief announcements regarding field trip reimbursements, Day on the Hill, and upcoming math events, the committee voted to enter executive session for negotiations.
